head.title: 1-01 Health worker density
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health worker density
head.meta.name: Density of health workers per 10 000 population
head.meta.numerator: Number of active health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation, by occupation and activity level
head.meta.definition:
Number of health workers per 10 000 population.
For activity level the following categories are recommended: practising health workers,
professionally active health workers, and health workers licensed to practise.
Total population as estimated in the World Population Prospects published by the Population
Division of the Department of Economic and Social Affairs of the United Nations Secretariat. In case
of other methodology used, WHO recalculates densities according to the UN population estimates in
order to harmonize the densities and ensure comparability.
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Activity level; Occupation
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: UN SDG 3.c.1, SDG 3.8.1, WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Working for Health programme, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), Immunization Agenda 2030 (IA2030), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE), Primary Health Care (PHC) Measurement Framework, Community Health Workers (CHWs), Global Oral Health Action Plan
head.meta.dataSources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Professional council/chamber/association registers; Labour force surveys; Population census data; United Nations Population Division

head.title: 1-02 Health worker density at subnational level
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health worker density at subnational level
head.meta.name: Density of active health workers per 10 000 population at subnational level
head.meta.numerator: Number of active health workers in level 1 subnational administrative units
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation
head.meta.definition:
Number of active health workers per 10 000 population in the given subnational administrative unit.
Preferably, the subnational unit should correspond to the place of work of health workers. The use
of administrative units to the first subnational level is recommended (depending on the structure
of administrative units and the size of subnational territories), without overlaps between the
administrative units. Examples of subnational administrative units include states, regions, provinces,
counties, and districts.
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Occupation; Subnational level
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: UN SDG 3.c.1, Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Working for Health programme, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE), Primary Health Care (PHC) Measurement Framework
head.meta.dataSources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Professional council/chamber/association registers; Population census data; Health facility database (with location); United Nations Population Division

head.title: 1-03 Health worker distribution by age group
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health worker distribution by age group
head.meta.name: Percentage of active health workers in different age groups
head.meta.numerator: Number of active health workers in age group categories
head.meta.denominator: Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation, by occupation and sex
head.meta.definition:
Percentage of active health workers in the given age and sex category.
This indicator enables to create the population pyramid of health workers. Age groups considered are
the following: < 25, 25–34, 35–44, 45–54, 55–64, ≥ 65 years. Sex groups corresponds to male or female
health workers.
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Age group; Sex; Occupation
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: UN SDG 3.c.1, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE)
head.meta.dataSources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Professional council/chamber/association registers; Labour force surveys; Population census data

head.title: 1-04 Health worker distribution by sex
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health worker distribution by sex
head.meta.name: Percentage of active health workers by sex
head.meta.numerator: Number of active health workers in sex categories
head.meta.denominator: Total number of active male and female health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation
head.meta.definition:
Percentage of active health workers in the given sex category.
Sex group corresponds to male or female health workers.
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Occupation; Sex
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: UN SDG 3.c.1, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE)
head.meta.dataSources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Labour force surveys; Population census data

head.title: 1-05 Health worker distribution by facility ownership
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health worker distribution by facility ownership
head.meta.name: Percentage of active health workers employed by facility ownership
head.meta.numerator: Number of active health workers, defined in headcounts, working in facilities owned by the given institutional sector (public or private not-for-profit or private for-profit)
head.meta.denominator: Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation
head.meta.definition:
Percentage of active health workers employed by facility ownership (public, private not-for-profit,
private for-profit).
The categories of facility ownership can be aligned to institutional sector definitions of the
System of National Accounts (SNA 2008).
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Facility/institution ownership type; Institutional sector
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE)
head.meta.dataSources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Labour force surveys; Census

head.title: 1-06 Health worker distribution by facility type
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health worker distribution by facility type
head.meta.name: Percentage of active health workers employed by facility type
head.meta.numerator: Number of active health workers, defined in headcounts, working in a specific facility type
head.meta.denominator: Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation
head.meta.definition:
Percentage of active health workers employed in the given facility type. Health facility
types are based on the classification of System of Health Accounts:
• Hospitals (HP.1)
• Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2)
• Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3)
• Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others)
• Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies)
• Providers of preventive care (HP.6)
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Facility type; Occupation
head.meta.dataSources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Labour Force Surveys; Census

head.title: 1-07 Health worker distribution by place of birth
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health worker distribution by place of birth
head.meta.name: Percentage of active health workers by their place of birth
head.meta.numerator: Number of active health workers by place of birth
head.meta.denominator: Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation
head.meta.definition:
Percentage of active health workers by their place of birth.
Place of birth is defined as national-born or foreign-born.
This indicator will capture the information on the health workers coming from abroad.
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Occupation; Place of birth
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM)
head.meta.dataSources: Health workforce registry or database; Professional council/chamber/association registers; Health facility data; Population census data

head.title: 1-08 Health worker distribution by place of training
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health worker distribution by place of training
head.meta.name: Percentage of active health workers by their place of training
head.meta.numerator: Number of active health workers by place of training
head.meta.denominator: Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation, by occupation and country of training among foreign-trained, by occupation and place of birth among foreign-trained
head.meta.definition:
Percentage of active health workers by their place of training.
Place of training is defined as either domestic-trained, foreign-trained or unknown location of training.
The disaggregation by occupation and country of training is applicable to foreign-trained workers,
and enables the monitoring of health worker migration by country of training. The disaggregation by
occupation and place of birth is applicable to foreign-trained workers, and enables the monitoring of
foreign-trained – national-born and foreign-trained – foreign-born workers.
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Occupation; Place of training
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM)
head.meta.dataSources: Health workforce registry or database; Professional council/chamber/association registers; Health facility data

head.title: 1-09 Annual inflows of health workers
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Annual inflows of health workers
head.meta.name: Ratio of newly active health workers to the total stock of active health workers
head.meta.numerator: Number of newly active health workers
head.meta.denominator: Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation, by occupation and place of training, by occupation, place of training and sex
head.meta.definition:
Newly active health workers are those who started their activity in the given profession. In case data
are available only for newly licensed health workers, the total number of licensed health workers
should be used as denominator regardless of availability of data on active health workers. For total
number of active health workers, data at the middle or the end of the reference year should be used.
Disaggregation by place of training (domestic-trained vs foreign-trained) enables to capture the
health labour market dynamics of migration.
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Newly active health worker; Activity level; Place of training; Sex; Occupation
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE)
head.meta.dataSources: Ministry of Health database; Health workforce registry or database; Professional council/chamber/association registers; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey)

head.title: 1-10 Annual outflows of health workers
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Annual outflows of health workers
head.meta.name: Ratio of active health workers leaving the health labour market to the total stock of active health workers
head.meta.numerator: Number of health workers who became inactive in the health labour market
head.meta.denominator: Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation, by occupation and type of exit (voluntary vs involuntary), by occupation, type of exit and sex
head.meta.definition:
Percentage of active health workers who became inactive in the health labour market
due to voluntary reason or involuntary reason
The disaggregation by type of exit has the following two categories:
• Voluntary exit corresponds to the following situations: emigration, temporary leave, change of
sector, early retirement or other voluntary reason. Only early retirement should be considered
as voluntary exit; retirement at standard age is to be counted in the involuntary exit.
• Involuntary exit corresponds to the following situations: death, retirement (excluding
early retirement), suspension from work, long-term illness or other involuntary reason.
For the total number of active health workers, data at the end of the previous year should be used.
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Activity level; Sex; Occupation
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE)
head.meta.dataSources: Health workforce registry or database; Professional council/chamber/association registers; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Data from pension and/or retirement administration units; Mortality records

head.title: 1-11 Vacancy rate
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Vacancy rate
head.meta.name: Ratio of unfilled posts to total number of funded posts
head.meta.numerator: Number of funded full-time posts that have not been filled for at least twelve months
head.meta.denominator: Total number of funded full-time posts (filled and unfilled)
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation
head.meta.definition:
Ratio of unfilled posts to total number of posts.
By limiting the count of unfilled posts for at least twelve months, this indicator enables to
distinguish between a systematic job vacancy situation versus potential rapid turnover of staff.
head.meta.glossary: Occupation; Job vacancy; Subnational level; Vacancy rate
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE)
head.meta.dataSources: Labour force surveys; Health facility assessments; Employment offices and/or job agencies

head.title: 1-12 Health worker distribution by type of contract
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health worker distribution by type of contract
head.meta.name: Percentage of active health workers by their type of contract
head.meta.numerator: Number of active health workers in specific types of contracts (full-time vs part-time)
head.meta.denominator: Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation
head.meta.definition:
Percentage of active health workers in the given type of contract.
Type of contract are defined as either full-time or part-time.
• Full-time workers are defined as employed or self-employed persons whose normal working hours
in their main job correspond at least to the legal number of working hours per week, i.e. usually
working 30 hours per week or above.
• Part-time workers are defined as employed or self-employed persons whose normal hours of
work are less than those of comparable full-time workers.
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Occupation; Contract type
head.meta.dataSources: Facility database and/or surveys; Health workforce registry or database; Labour force surveys; Public service human resources and payroll administrations

head.title: 2-01 Health workforce education and training capacity
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health workforce education and training capacity
head.meta.name: Ratio of health workforce education and training capacity per 10 000 population
head.meta.numerator: Number of places in health education and training institutions
head.meta.disaggregation: By health workforce education and training programme
head.meta.definition:
The health workforce education and training capacity refers to the number of places or seats.
This indicator enables to estimate the availability of the training capacity and express it per
10 000 population.
Total population as estimated in the World Population Prospects by the United Nations Population
Division. In case of other methodology used, WHO recalculates densities according to the UN
population estimates in order to harmonize the densities and ensure comparability.
head.meta.glossary: Health workforce education and training capacity; Health workforce education and training programme; Health workforce education and training institution
head.meta.dataSources: Ministry of Education; Data on education and training statistics; Education and training institutions; United Nations Population Division

head.title: 2-02 Ratio of applications to education and training capacity
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Ratio of applications to education and training capacity
head.meta.name: Ratio of applications for health workforce education and training to the training capacity
head.meta.numerator: Number of applications for the first year of a health workforce education and training programme
head.meta.denominator: Total number of places available in the first year of a health workforce education and training programme
head.meta.disaggregation: By health workforce education and training programme, by health workforce education and training programme and sex
head.meta.definition:
Applications for the first year of a health workforce education and training programme divided
by the number of training places for this first year.
head.meta.glossary: Health workforce education and training place; Health workforce education and training programme; Applications; Sex
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM)
head.meta.dataSources: Ministry of Education; Ministry of Higher Education; Databases on education and training statistics; education and training institutions

head.title: 2-03 Ratio of enrolments to application
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Ratio of enrolments to application
head.meta.name: Ratio of students enrolled in the first year of health workforce education and training programmes to applications for these programmes
head.meta.numerator: Total number of enrolments in the first year of a health workforce education and training programme
head.meta.denominator: Total number of applications for the first year of a health workforce education and training programme
head.meta.disaggregation: By health workforce education and training programme, by health workforce education and training programme and sex
head.meta.definition: Ratio of enrolment in health workforce education and training programmes to applications.
head.meta.glossary: Applications; Enrolments; Health workforce education and training programme; Sex
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM)
head.meta.dataSources: Databases on education statistics; Education and training institutions

head.title: 2-04 Ratio of graduates to stock
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Ratio of graduates to stock
head.meta.name: Ratio of graduates of health workforce education and training programmes to the stock of active health workers
head.meta.numerator: Number of graduates from a cohort of a health workforce education and training programme
head.meta.denominator: Number of active health workers, defined in headcounts
head.meta.disaggregation: By health workforce education and training programme, by health workforce education and training programme and sex, by health workforce education and training programme and health education and training institution ownership (public/private)
head.meta.definition:
This indicator aims to approach the graduation rate using data available on an annual basis. The exact
graduation rate can also be calculated from longitudinal information on students following cohorts
of students. If such data are available, the graduation rate estimated from the most recent complete
cohort can be reported. In addition to the total number of graduates, distribution of graduates by sex
and by ownership enables to identify potential maldistribution and inequities.
head.meta.glossary: Graduate; Health workforce education and training programme; Sex; Student; Active health worker
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Working for Health programme, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE)
head.meta.dataSources: Databases of health education and training institutions; Health workforce registry or database; Professional council/chamber/association registers

head.title: 2-05 Duration of education and training
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Duration of education and training
head.meta.name: Duration of health workforce education and training programmes, in years
head.meta.disaggregation: By health workforce education and training programme
head.meta.definition:
Duration of health workforce education and training is the number of years required to complete
a full curriculum for each health workforce education and training programme. This duration does
not include specializations or time to obtain additional, optional, certifications.
head.meta.glossary: Health workforce education and training programme; Duration of health workforce education and training
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM)
head.meta.dataSources: Ministry of Education; Database on education and training statistics; Education and training institutions

head.title: 2-06 Accreditation mechanisms for education and training institutions and their programmes
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Accreditation mechanisms for education and training institutions and their programmes
head.meta.name: Existence of national and/or subnational mechanisms for accreditation of health workforce education and training institutions and their programmes (Yes/Partial/No)
head.meta.disaggregation: By health workforce education and training programme
head.meta.definition:
The following questions should guide a response to this indicator:
• Have national and/or subnational mechanisms for accreditation of health workforce education
and training institutions and their programmes been established?
• Are national and/or subnational mechanisms for accreditation of health workforce education
and training institutions and their programmes compulsory?
• Are there national and/or subnational mechanisms for accreditation of health workforce
education and training institutions and their programmes that are not compulsory?
• If established, do national and/or subnational mechanisms for accreditation of health workforce
education and training institutions and their programmes take into account national education
plans for the health workforce?
head.meta.glossary: Accreditation; Health workforce education and training programme; Health workforce education and training institution
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Working for Health programme, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), Primary Health Care (PHC) Measurement Framework
head.meta.dataSources: Ministry of Health; Ministries of Education, Higher Education or similar; National accreditation authorities; Legitimate bodies, statutory corporations; Professional council/chamber/association registers

head.title: 2-07 Standards for education and training programmes
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Standards for education and training programmes
head.meta.name: Existence of standards for education and training programmes
head.meta.disaggregation: By health workforce education and training programme (for all but last sub-indicator 2-07.7)
head.meta.definition:
This indicator is a composite of seven sub-indicators, see below. The response to these seven
sub-indicators is aggregated as a score (see part II on methods) on a scale from 1 (nascent) to 5
(sustainable).
Each sub-indicator is a self-assessment of one aspect of standards on education and training
programmes. To help answer these self-assessed sub-indicators, a series of guiding questions
are provided.
head.meta.glossary: Health workforce education and training programme; Accreditation; Accreditation systems; Social accountability; Social determinants of health; Interprofessional education; Continuing professional development; Lifelong learning; Occupation; In-service training
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), Primary Health Care (PHC) Measurement Framework, Community Health Workers (CHWs)
head.meta.dataSources: Ministry of Health; Ministries of Education, Higher Education or similar; National accreditation authorities; Legitimate bodies, statutory corporations; Professional council/chamber/association registers; Ministries responsible for labour

head.meta.name: Total expenditure on compensation of health workers

head.meta.definition:
Total expenditure expressed in US$ on compensation of health workers.
If possible, disaggregation by public or private sources for the compensation of health workers.

head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM)

head.title: 3-02 Entry-level wages and salaries
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Entry-level wages and salaries
head.meta.name: Average entry-level wage and salary excluding social contributions
head.meta.disaggregation: By occupation, by occupation and public/private
head.meta.definition:
Average wage or salary in US$ received by health workers when entering the active health

head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Occupation; Remuneration; Wage and salary
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM)
head.meta.dataSources: Ministry of Health records; Ministry of Finance records; Payroll data; Income tax data; General labour force surveys; Specific health worker surveys

head.title: 3-03 Total expenditure on health workforce education
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Total expenditure on health workforce education
head.meta.name: Total expenditure on health workforce pre-service education (current and capital)
head.meta.disaggregation: By health workforce education and training programme, by health workforce education and training programme and institution ownership (public/private)
head.meta.definition:
Total expenditure in US$ on health workforce education (current and capital). The disaggregation

Education here refers to pre-service education and does not include in-service education and training.
head.meta.glossary: Total public expenditure; Pre-service education
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM)
head.meta.dataSources: Integrated Financial Management Information System; Ministry of Finance; Ministry of Health; Ministry of Education; Ministry of Defence (expenditure on military HWF education may fall under the Ministry of Defence budget); Education Management Information System: Ministry of (Higher) Education; ministry or other accredited bodies responsible for technical and vocational education and training; National Bureau of Statistics – Government financial statistics departments; System of Health Accounts; National Education Accounts

head.title: 3-04 Expenditure per graduate on health workforce education
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Expenditure per graduate on health workforce education
head.meta.name: Expenditure per graduate of health workforce education and training programme
head.meta.numerator: Total expenditure on health workforce education
head.meta.denominator: Total number of graduates from health workforce education and training programmes
head.meta.disaggregation: By health workforce education and training programme, by health workforce education and training programme and institution ownership (public/private)
head.meta.definition:
Expenditure in US$ on health workforce education per graduate.
The disaggregation by programme enables to identify inequities across programmes.
The disaggregation by institution ownership enables to distinguish between publicly
and privately owned education institutions.
head.meta.glossary: Health workforce education and training programme; Graduate; Total expenditure on health workforce education
head.meta.dataSources: Integrated Financial Management Information System: Ministry of Finance; Ministry of Health; Ministry of Education; Ministry of Defence (expenditure on military HWF education may fall under this budget); Education Management Information System: Ministry of (Higher) Education; ministry or other accredited body responsible for technical and vocational education and training; National Bureau of Statistics – Government financial statistics departments; System of Health Accounts; National Education Accounts

Average tuition fee in US$ per student enrolled in health workforce education and training per year,

head.title: 4-01 Labour regulations and policies for health workforce

head.meta.definition:

head.title: 4-02 Health workforce governance and leadership capacity
head.meta.module: Module 4: Working conditions, governance and leadership
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Health workforce governance and leadership capacity
head.meta.name: Existence of health workforce governance and leadership capacity at national and/or subnational levels
head.meta.definition:
This indicator is a composite of five sub-indicators, see below. The response to these five
sub-indicators is aggregated as a score (see part II on methods) on a scale from 1 (nascent)
to 5 (sustainable).
Each sub-indicator is a self-assessment of one aspect of countries’ governance and leadership
capacity vis-à-vis of health and care workers. To help answer these self-assessed sub-indicators,
a series of guiding questions are provided.
head.meta.glossary: Occupation; Health workforce planning; Lifelong learning; Continuing professional development; In-service training
head.meta.reportingFrameworks: Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Working for Health programme, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM)
head.meta.dataSources: Ministry of Health, Education, Labour; Regional and/or subnational ministries of health and education; Institutions or units responsible for policies on health workforce; Relevant ministries according to the national government structure and constitutional arrangements/ level of devolution; Educational institutions; Health facilities

head.title: 4-03 Share of women in leadership role
head.meta.module: Module 4: Working conditions, governance and leadership
head.meta.abbreviatedName: Share of women in leadership role
head.meta.name: Share of women in senior management positions in the Ministry of Health
head.meta.numerator: Number of women in leadership roles in the Ministry of Health, defined in headcounts
head.meta.denominator: Total number of men and women in leadership roles in the Ministry of Health, defined in headcounts
head.meta.definition:
Share of women, expressed as a percentage, of women in senior management positions in
the Ministry of Health.
To monitor and report on this indicator, it is advised to count all individuals at director-level
or equivalent positions within the Ministry of Health. Using the organigram of the Ministry of
Health, focusing on the senior positions, should be sufficient to estimate this indicator. Alternative
approaches could be based on the count of men and women in delegations participating to the
annual World Health Assemblies.
head.meta.glossary: Active health worker; Leadership role; Gender
head.meta.dataSources: Ministry of Health organigram or official documents

head.title: 4-04 International Health Regulations implementation capacity
head.meta.module: Module 4: Working conditions, governance and leadership
head.meta.abbreviatedName: International Health Regulations implementation capacity
head.meta.name: Availability of human resources to implement International Health Regulations core capacity requirements (None/Limited/Developed/Demonstrated/ Sustainable)
head.meta.definition:
This indicator is based on indicator D3.2 of the Joint External Evaluation (JEE) tool, third edition
(which is similar to indicator C6.1 in State Party Self-assessment Annual Reporting (SAPR) tool),
and it uses the following (capability) items:
No capacity (level 1)
Country does not have appropriate human resources capacity in relevant sectors required
to detect, assess, notify, report and respond to events according to IHR provisions
Limited capacity (level 2)
Appropriate human resources are available in some relevant sectors at the national level
to detect, assess, notify, report and respond to events according to IHR provisions
Developed capacity (level 3)
Appropriate human resources are available in all relevant sectors at national and intermediate
levels to detect, assess, notify, report and respond to events according to IHR provisions
Demonstrated capacity (level 4)
Human resources are available as required in all relevant sectors at the national, intermediate
and primary public health levels to detect, assess, notify, report and respond to events according
to IHR provisions
Sustainable capacity (level 5)
Country has documented policies or procedures for sustainable appropriate human resources in all
relevant sectors to detect, assess, notify, report and respond to events according to IHR provisions,
that are exercised (as applicable), reviewed, evaluated and updated on a regular basis, and country
may assist other countries in planning and developing human resources for IHR implementation,
to the extent possible

head.title: 4-05 National capacity to monitor key metrics for health workforce planning and global monitoring frameworks
head.meta.module: Module 4: Working conditions, governance and leadership
head.meta.abbreviatedName: National capacity to monitor key metrics for health workforce planning and global monitoring frameworks
head.meta.name: Capacity of national human resources for health information systems to monitor key metrics relevant for national health workforce planning and policy-making and for global monitoring frameworks
head.meta.definition:
This indicator is a composite of nine sub-indicators, see below. The response to these nine
sub-indicators is aggregated as a score (see part II on methods) on a scale from 1 (nascent)
to 5 (sustainable).
Each sub-indicator is a self-assessment of one aspect of the capacity of the national human
resources for health information system (HRHIS) or other mechanisms to report on key metrics
that are relevant for national health workforce planning and policy-making as well as for global
monitoring frameworks. To help answer some of these self-assessed sub-indicators, guiding
questions are provided.
